rows.en: {f:There it was|……}!{p}

Two eyeballs, floating about ten centimeters from {f:my|my} shoulder.
Their dark irises were staring at {f:me|me}.
Forgetting even to scream, {f:I|I} stared back at {f:the thing|it}.
My head swam with a wave of dizziness.
The strength drained out of my legs.
It seemed I'd lost control of my body again.
The instant I started to black out, the eyeballs leapt into {f:my|my} mouth.{p}

But the eyeballs didn't care about any of that; they kept shoving their way in, deeper and deeper.
I couldn't make a sound.
I couldn't breathe.
It hurt so much that tears came.{p}

And at last, the smooth eyeballs were forced down into the back of my throat.
...Strangely, I didn't feel sick anymore.{p}

My mind went blank, and I felt so sleepy I could hardly stand it.
Maybe I should just fall asleep like this.
{f:I|I} curled up on the floor and hugged my knees.
I heard someone's voice.
Sleep... sleep...
That body of yours... I'll be taking it...
...Whose voice was that?
Had {f:I|I} {f:fallen|fallen} into the trap of some demon that nested in this school?
...But I didn't care anymore{f:|}.
{f:I|I} was sleepy{f:|}.
I'd just go to sleep like this{f:|}... forever.
In the moment I drifted off, I felt something evil, a wicked will, inside my body.
But what that meant...{p}{f:I|I} no longer had the strength even to think about it.{p}

Hosoda had come back for me{f:|}.
I stood up, and the door opened in front of {f:me|me}.{p}

"Still haven't changed your mind?"
It was Hosoda, just as I'd thought{f:|}.
Before I could freeze up again, I hurried over to him.
"{f:I'm|I'm} coming too!"{p}

Hosoda nodded, looking relieved.
I see. That's good.
Then let's head for the restroom where they say Hanako-san appears.
On the way, I'll tell you a story.
A story about Hanako-san.{p}

Wow, that's really something.
I'm not being sarcastic.
For me, it's rarer NOT to get a failing grade.
I envy you.
Anyway, shall I go on with the story?{p}

You don't remember?
Are you maybe the type who never learns their lesson?
The type who gets called in for a failing grade and just goes home anyway?
If so, you'd better quit doing that.
It's not about getting chewed out by the teachers or anything like that.{p}

Why, you ask...
That time, there were six students kept behind.
Four boys and two girls.
But there were seven students who'd gotten failing grades.
Even so, the last one never showed up.
...A lot like us today, isn't it?{p}

Oh, okay.
That's for the best.{p}

Don't.
I'm not trying to be mean to you or anything.
It's better if you don't go.{p}...But if you absolutely insist on going, I won't stop you anymore.
On second thought, I won't go
I really have to go

...All right.
But be careful, okay?
With that, Hosoda fell silent.
He was watching {f:me|me} with a strange look in his eyes.
I had a bad feeling about it, but {f:I|I} stood up.{p}
I stepped out into the creaking hallway.{p}{f:Now|Now}, which way was the restroom{f:|}?
Right
Left
{f:I|I} decided to try going right.{p}

I could feel the floor sink whenever I put my weight on it.
If I wasn't careful, the floorboards might really snap and I'd fall right through.{p}

I moved forward carefully, one step at a time.
But when I reached the end of the dark hallway, {f:I|I} was let down.{p}

It was a dead end.
There was no restroom anywhere.
Was it on the other side{f:|}?
With that thought, I turned around.{p}

...Hosoda was right in front of me.
"There's no restroom this way.
Let's go back now."
He said it in a gentle voice, as if he hadn't noticed that {f:I|I} was so startled I'd nearly stopped breathing.
{f:I|I} nodded without a word.
That shock had killed any urge to go to the restroom {f:I'd had|I'd had}.{p}

{f:Hosoda and I|Hosoda and I} went back to the classroom where we'd been.
And then the story picked up where it had left off.{p}
{f:I|I} decided to try going left.{p}

Skulls, lots of them, set into the wall.
The hair on the back of my neck stood on end.
...But {f:I|I} soon realized my mistake.
They weren't skulls.
They were stains on the wall{f:|}.
They were shaped like human faces.
But for so many stains to all have the exact same shape...
It felt eerie{f:|}.
{f:I|I} went closer and took a good look at the stains.{p}

Before I knew it, Hosoda was standing there.
"N-no, um... I just thought the stains moved a second ago."
As I said it, a sudden wave of embarrassment welled up in me.
Stains, moving?
It was like a frightened child seeing a curtain sway and deciding it was a ghost{f:|}.
{f:I'd seen things only because I was so scared|Maybe I'd seen things only because I was so scared}.
"...It's nothing."
"Is that so?
Then let's go back."{p}

{f:I|I} nodded and went back to the classroom with Hosoda.
And then the story picked up where it had left off.{p}

Are you serious?
They'd been there the whole time since classes ended.
They'd be getting hungry, and it'd be getting dark outside the windows...
And yet not one of the six noticed.
However you look at it, that's not normal.
If you don't think so, then either {f:you're the weird one|you just answered any old way}, or {f:you're seriously contrary|you're making fun of me}.
{f:If you want to mess up my story that badly|How mean}, {f:suit yourself|I'm being serious about this story, you know}.
{f:I'm going to keep on talking anyway|Please don't ruin the mood}.
...Anyway, they all started to think something was wrong.{p}

Right?
They thought so too.{p}

That's when they should have just agreed to go home.
But that's not what happened.
Instead, all the blame fell on the seventh one, the one who never came.
Well, you can understand how they felt.
They were all supposed to go through this together, and one of them got to run off.
So they forgot all about the make-up class and turned it into a badmouthing session.
This is what's wrong with him, that's what I hate about him, that sort of thing.{p}
While they were really getting into it, there was a loud clunk.{p}
Wondering what was going on, they peeked out the door.{p}And then... what do you think they found?
A school bag
Nothing at all

There was a school bag lying in the hallway.
Someone picked it up and said,
"This is his bag."
...Just like that.
That's right, it was the seventh one's bag.
Had he overheard them badmouthing him?
The six looked at each other.
They must have thought they were in trouble.{p}

When they stuck their heads out into the hallway, someone ducked out of sight on the stair landing.
It was the seventh guy.
After all the awful things they'd said about him, he must not have been able to bring himself to come in.
Meaning to apologize, they all went out after him.{p}
There was no one on the landing anymore.{p}

But they heard a noise from farther up the stairs.
He must have gone upstairs.
That's what they all thought.
And just as they started up after him...
Something dropped at their feet with a heavy plop.
A tube-shaped thing, about forty-five centimeters long.{p}
One of them went to pick it up, and screamed.{p}

It was a human arm.
It had been chopped clean off at the elbow.{p}

The girls screamed too.
But one of them, keeping a cool head, pointed at it.
"Isn't that fake?"
...Just like that.
Now that it was pointed out, there wasn't a single drop of blood on the cut end.
The color was kind of whitish, too.
"It's him!"{p}

There was only one person who'd pull something like this.
That seventh guy.
Furious, they all started up the stairs.
And then something else fell.{p}

When they looked, this time it was the other arm.
Of course, something like that didn't scare them anymore.
"Knock it off!"
"We know it's you!"
Shouting things like that, they went on up the stairs.{p}

When they got up to the third floor, the restroom light was on.
Did he think he'd hidden himself by running in there?
With the light on, he was obviously going to get caught right away.
They started walking toward the restroom.
Then something inside the restroom toppled over.
It fell out into the hallway and lay there in plain sight in front of them.{p}

It was a leg, from the knee down.
They all snickered.
If he meant to be hiding, they thought, it was a ridiculously stupid way to go about it.
"Come on, cut it out.
We all know it's you..."
The one saying that peeked into the restroom, and the voice broke off in the middle.{p}

There was no one inside the restroom.
No one, only the other leg, lying there in the cold, pale light.
"Hee hee hee..."
Just then, they heard laughter behind them.{p}

After all, her face was covered by a pure white mask.
But at the very least, the eyes peering out of that mask weren't laughing.
And she had him with her.
The seventh one.
When they saw him, someone let out a shrill scream.
His arms and legs were gone, cut off at the joints.
The woman's mouth seemed to twist into a grin.
And then she ripped his head off, his eyes squeezed tightly shut.
...The blood that should have sprayed everywhere never came, not a single drop.
Just like a wax figure.{p}
All the six of them could do was stare at the mask of the woman as she came closer.{p}

...So what became of those six, you ask?
...They were never found.
The next day, the teacher who'd gone home and left them in the make-up class and the teacher who'd been asked to take over both searched the old school building before the problem could get any bigger.
But they didn't find their bodies, or even a single drop of blood.
And those two teachers got their stories straight: they said they'd sent the students home properly.
Awful, isn't it?
And so the six were listed as missing.
In the end, no one ever saw any of them again.
Still, their classmates knew the six who vanished had stayed behind at school for a make-up class.
And since they disappeared right after that, strange rumors started going around.{p}

Strange moans could be heard from the girls' restroom on the third floor of the old school building, someone saw the missing students there; all sorts of weird rumors spread.
And so the story became that it was Hanako-san's curse.
That Hanako-san had taken the six away.
Whether those six strayed into another world, or whether it really was Hanako-san's curse, nobody can say.{p}

But the one I feel sorry for is the seventh one.
Unlike the other six, nobody knew he'd been in the old school building, so he was treated differently.
He was a bit of a delinquent, so people even suspected he'd run away from home.
Talk about adding insult to injury.
But... why would he come back so late like that?
If he was skipping the make-up class, he could've just gone straight home.
...Maybe he'd been there from the very beginning.
And Hanako-san caught him.
Right above the heads of everyone taking the make-up class, Hanako-san may have been hacking him to pieces...
...And that's the end of the story about the old school building.
Mind you, nobody actually saw them being killed, so it's not very believable.{p}
That's right, there was nothing there.{p}

When they stuck their heads out into the hallway, someone ducked out of sight on the stair landing.
So they all...{p}

...Just as I thought, there was nothing.
Fighting down a bad feeling, I stuck my head out into the hallway.{p}

A figure ducked out of sight on the landing.
That's impossible.
It was happening just like in Hosoda's story.
{f:I|I} rushed out into the hallway.
I wanted to see who that figure really was.{p}

There was no one on the landing anymore.
{f:Upstairs, maybe|Upstairs, maybe}?{p}

The one strangling me was a girl with a bobbed haircut.
She wore a pure white mask, so I couldn't see her face.
Her eyes glinted coldly.
Who {f:are you|are you}★
I tried to ask, but no voice came out.
For just an instant, the girl's eyes softened.{p}

And the next instant, I heard a heavy, dull crack.
What was that sound{f:|}?
As {f:I|I} wondered, my head lolled and swung around.
Warm liquid gushed from my nose and mouth.
Ah... that was the sound of {f:my|my} neck breaking{f:|, wasn't it}.{p}By the time I realized it, {f:I|I} had already been dragged down into darkness.{p}

"See? It's just an ordinary clock, nothing unusual about it."
Saying that, he showed {f:me|me} the clock.
"I guess so..."
Reaching out to take it, {f:I|I} saw it and pulled my hand back.{p}

On the back of the clock, the side opposite the face, black clumps {f:were|were} stuck thick all over it.
And they were squirming.{p}

I {f:looked|looked} at Hosoda in a panic.
He was gazing blankly at {f:me|me}.
Couldn't he see these black things{f:|}?
Even though, bit by bit, the clumps were breaking apart and crawling along his fingers and up his arm?{p}

"What's the matter, {a}{f:|}?
I got a really good scary story ready just for you."
As he spoke, the black things were crawling up to his chest.
They were bugs{f:|}.
Tiny bugs like flying ants, thousands upon thousands of them, swarming together{f:|}.
"You're a strange one."
As Hosoda said that, black winged bugs spilled out of his mouth in clumps.
{f:I|I} couldn't believe my eyes.
But the bugs kept spilling from the puzzled Hosoda's mouth and nostrils.
With a rip, a split opened in his cheek.
And bugs came gushing out of that split, too.
By now, Hosoda's whole body was black, buried in crawling bugs.
And still, Hosoda kept on talking.{p}

"Aw, come on. Come over here."
A pitch-black hand grabbed {f:me|me}.
In no time, dozens of bugs crawled over onto {f:my|my} arm.
Goosebumps broke out all over me.
I tried to shake him off, but with {f:my|my} strength there was nothing I could do.
Worse, Hosoda pulled {f:me|me} closer.
"You know, I've taken a liking to you.
I'm sure we can be good friends."
His other hand wrapped around {f:my|my} shoulders.{p}

The pitch-black face loomed right up close.
Hundreds of bugs crawled all over {f:my|my} body.
It prickled and stung.
They were biting into my skin{f:|}.
Trying to burrow inside my body★
{f:I|I} thrashed, trying to brush off both Hosoda and the bugs.
But the strength went out of my knees.
Oh no!
So the bugs had been biting to paralyze {f:my|my} body{f:|}...
{f:I|I} slowly toppled over.
Right by my ears came a rustling, the sound of countless wings rubbing together.
The bugs {f:would crawl|came crawling} into {f:my|my} body.
They would devour what was inside, multiply, and become a black mass wearing {f:my|my} skin.
Yes, just like Hosoda.
In the end, I never did solve the mystery of the old school building{f:|}.
It struck me as funny that I was thinking about such things right up until I died.{p}Letting out a sigh that was almost a laugh, {f:I|I} lost consciousness.{p}
...Go on, get closer.{p}
